system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Figure 7 in Appendix A presents the System Prompt we designed for the action prediction step.
system_prompt_style.note: Paper only; no mechanism for how the system prompt is built. Appendix A is not in the evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: At every step, the agent receives the current screenshot, auxiliary text, and history as inputs
env_context_strategy.note: The agent navigates the live web with browser actions. Per-step observations are screenshots plus element text.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: we perform context clipping to remove outdated web page information and only keep the three most recent observations in the inputs, and we keep the entire history of thoughts and actions
context_compaction.note: Observations are elided while thoughts and actions are kept, so this is closest to tool_output_pruning.

observation_format.evidence_quote: we overlay bounding boxes of the interactive elements on the websites to better guide the agent's action prediction.
observation_format.note: Also auxiliary element text. The accessibility-tree text-only variant is a baseline, not the default.

tool_call_format.note: Paper says only 'a concise Action Format'. No parser code is available.

tool_count.evidence_quote: 1) Click. This action involves clicking on an element within a webpage
tool_count.note: Count of the 7 actions in Sec. 3.4: Click, Input, Scroll, Wait, Back, Jump to Search Engine, Answer. They are actions, not function schemas.

edit_primitive.note: Web agent; no file-editing tool is discussed. No code is available.

protocol_standardization.note: Paper only; no dependency list is available.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Inspired by the paradigm of ReAct Prompting (Yao et al., 2022b), we also prompt our agent to generate a thought process first before generating the action code.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: we also prompt our agent to generate a thought process first before generating the action code.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: In contrast, WebV oyager does not require any additional modules.

delegation_mechanism.note: No code or registry is available.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: managing the entire process end-to-end without any intermediate human intervention.
human_in_loop.note: The paper states the absence outright.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: which consist of historical ac- tions ai and observations oi

self_verification.note: The GPT-4V auto-evaluator is offline benchmark evaluation, not in-loop verification. No harness code is available.

retry_policy.note: Step-level regeneration on execution errors is noted in Sec. 3.3. Task retries are not discussed.

rollback.note: The Back action is page navigation, not rollback.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: until the model generates a terminating action or the maximum step is reached.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: We develop an automated web-browsing environ- ment using Selenium3.
execution_isolation.note: The Selenium browser is inferred to run on the host. Isolation is not stated.

network_policy.evidence_quote: we do not host any websites locally and allow the agent to explore the open web instead

tracing.note: Screenshots are saved for evaluation. The trace format is unknown.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: we propose an automated evaluation protocol using GPT-4V .
eval_hooks.note: Paper only. Presence of the evaluator in the repo is not verified.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a multi- modal web agent designed to autonomously ac- complish web tasks online from start to finish

open_source.note: The paper promises code release. No LICENSE is in the evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we incorporate two additional backbone models, namely Claude 3 Opus (Anthropic, 2024) and GPT- 4o
model_agnostic.note: Multiple vendors are used. No abstraction layer is shown.

primary_artifact.note: Only the paper is in the evidence.
